I look at my classmates who are genuinely excited about VLSI design, and I feel like an absolute imposter who has wasted four years of life. I'm turning 22 next month and I feel like my life is already over before it even started.

Every time I open LinkedIn, it's the same thing: 'I am thrilled to share that I have started a new position at...' while I am sitting here with three backlogs in my fifth semester. My roommate already got a pre-placement offer and is planning his life, while I can't even get out of bed to attend my 9 AM lectures. I feel like a ghost watching everyone else move forward in a high-speed train while I'm stuck on a platform that doesn't exist.

I got my results back and I topped my batch in DBMS. But I didn't feel a thing. I just stared at the grade sheet, went back to my PG, and slept for 14 hours. We grind for these marks, then we grind for the interview, then we grind for the corporate appraisal... when does the actual living start? I feel like I'm just a machine running on a battery that's slowly leaking acid.

It's 3 AM and I'm looking at my old sketchbooks from high school. I used to paint every day. Now my hands only know how to type terminal commands and debug C++ code that I don't even care about. I feel like I sold my soul for the promise of financial stability, but I've lost the only version of myself that I actually liked. I don't even know who is looking back at me in the mirror anymore.

I just got a 9.2 CGPA this semester, and my LinkedIn is full of people getting SWE-2 offers at FAANG. My parents keep asking why I haven't cracked a 30 LPA package yet. I'm sitting in my room practicing DFS and BFS on LeetCode, and I just started crying out of nowhere. I don't even want this. I feel like I'm running a marathon on a treadmill—exhausted, moving fast, but staying in the exact same meaningless spot. What is the point of all this grind if I feel so completely dead inside?

Everyone in my batch seems to have their life figured out. They're talking about MS in the US, or core engineering jobs, or UPSC prep. I chose ECE because my dad said it had scope, but I hate it. I have three backlogs, my coding skills are nonexistent, and graduation is in four months. I literally sit during lectures just staring at the fan, wondering how I messed up my life so early. I’m only twenty-one, but it feels like my future is already a dead end.

I finished my midterms today and actually did pretty well. But when I got back to my hostel room, I just stared at the ceiling for three hours. I look at my seniors who got placed—they work 12 hours a day, post corporate jargon on LinkedIn, and spend their weekends drinking just to forget the week. Is this the prize? I'm killing myself studying DSA and system design just to become a cog in some corporate machine that doesn't care about me. I feel so hollow, like I'm grieving a life I haven't even started living yet.

Tomorrow is my 22nd birthday and I’ve never felt more pathetic. My school friends are posting pictures of their new cars, or their tech startup fundings, or trips to Europe. Meanwhile, I'm stuck in my third year of college with a mediocre CGPA, no internships lined up, and zero passion for anything. I don’t even know what I like anymore because I spent my whole youth just trying to survive school and college exams. I feel like an NPC in my own life, just watching everyone else play the main character.

My uncle's son just got a package of 45 LPA at an investment bank. Now, every dinner at my house is a quiet trial where my parents look at me like I'm a failed investment. I'm preparing for campus placements, but my mind goes completely blank during mock interviews because the pressure is choking me. I don't even care about the money; I just want to write music or do something creative, but that's a luxury I can't afford because we are middle class. I feel trapped in a life that was designed for me by my family's financial anxieties.

I cracked the 12 LPA offer yesterday. My parents are busy calling everyone, boasting about it. But I spent the last three hours locked in the bathroom, crying. I worked so hard for this, cleared all the DSA rounds, kept my CGPA at 8.9, and now that it’s here, I feel absolutely nothing. Just this hollow, terrifying emptiness. Is this it? Is this the prize for running myself into the ground for four years?

I turn twenty-two next week and my LinkedIn feed is a graveyard of my own self-esteem. Everyone from my batch is posting about their SDE-1 roles, system design certifications, or MS admissions, and here I am, unable to even choose a project topic for my final semester because I'm terrified I'll lock myself into a career I hate. I feel like I'm standing on a train platform watching every single train leave while I just freeze. What if I make the wrong choice and waste my entire life?

I failed my DSA mock interview today and my dad just looked at me and asked why I couldn't be more like my cousin who got into FAANG. I have midterms next week, three backlogs from last sem I'm trying to clear, and I can't even get out of bed. I feel like an absolute fraud, just coasting along while everyone else is actually going somewhere. I’m just so incredibly tired of trying to live up to a version of me that doesn't even exist.

I spent the last two years grinding for a branch change to CS, and now that I'm here, I absolutely hate it. I sit in these lectures about compiler design and database management, looking at the screen, and I feel this physical ache in my chest because I realize I don't care about any of this. I used to love writing and sketching, but I buried all of that to get a 'stable' branch, and now I don't even know who I am anymore. Did I destroy my own soul for a corporate package?

Only two months left until graduation and everyone is celebrating, but I just feel this cold, paralyzing dread. The thought of moving to a new city, finding an apartment, working 9-to-5 under some boss who doesn't care about me, and doing that day in and day out until I die... it feels like a trap. Is this what adulting is? Just sacrificing your freedom to pay bills and pretend you're happy on weekends?

I just finished my 5th semester DSA lab exam. Everyone is talking about Amazon and Microsoft placements, and my dad keeps sending me LinkedIn screenshots of my cousin who landed a 40 LPA package. I have an 8.9 CGPA, I do the prep, but honestly? I feel nothing. Just this hollow, terrifying void. I'm running so hard but I don't even know what I'm running towards anymore. If this is what the rest of my life is—chasing numbers and packages—I don't think I want to do it.

I'm graduating in three months. I spent four years grinding for this B.Tech, clearing backlogs, staying up for midterms, and now that the placement offer is finally in my inbox, I locked myself in the bathroom and cried. It’s a great MNC role, but I feel like an absolute fraud. I don't care about software architecture or scaling databases. I feel like I've built this entire fake persona to please my parents and now I'm trapped in it forever.

Every night I scroll through Instagram and LinkedIn and it feels like everyone has their life figured out. Some friend from my first-semester batch is starting an NGO, someone else is in Munich for their MS, and here I am, failing my DBMS mock interviews and eating cold Maggi at 3 AM. I'm turning 22 next week and I feel like a complete waste of space. Why did I ever think I could make something of myself?

I changed my major twice and I still feel completely lost. My parents are constantly asking about my future, comparing me to my elder sister who cleared UPSC on her first attempt. I sit in these lectures on compiler design and my brain just shuts down. I want to pack a bag and leave, but I have no money, no concrete plans, and this paralyzing fear that if I fail at this, I’ll prove everyone who doubted me right.

I hit all my goals. 9.2 CGPA, cleared the coding rounds, got the high-paying SDE-1 offer during the first week of placements. But ever since the announcement, I've felt this massive wave of exhaustion and sadness. I thought landing this would make me happy, but I just feel numb. Is this it? Is the rest of my life just waking up, writing code for a tech giant, and waiting to grow old? I feel so ungrateful but I'm deeply terrified of this mundane reality.
